svg.text: One flow as a hexagon: the domain service, its ports (traits, dashed yellow), the adapters behind them, and the data plane they start
TransferService<S, A, F, D, C, E>
Provider side of the transfer process: request, start,
suspend, complete, terminate; checks the agreement and its
policy; a request that comes while the finalization event is
on its way proves it arrived (settle_finalization_on_its_way,
ADR 0007); a repeated request gets the transfer it already has
Load and save transfers; find a
New ids and the current time
Start and stop the data flow;
Tests: the same adapter in memory
Speaks Data Plane Signaling to the
data plane; a repeated signal counts
as done. Names the source in metadata
Built-in data plane: a bearer token
per pull flow (only its hash is kept,
with an expiry); a PushJob per push
Flows with source, token hash, push
data with its bearer token; refused when the
consumer's membership no longer holds, cut
One switch per flow: suspend and
AccessGate for the data plane: checks
s3:// sources: a GET signed with
Push: one POST of the source to the
consumer's endpoint with its token; started
source_if_authorized(id, token), then fetch the source
C4 model, level 4. Solid arrows: uses. Dashed arrows: implements. Without the data-plane feature, NoDataFlows (transfer.rs) stands behind DataFlows and every transfer is refused.
The steps the four process services share (receive with proof of delivery, compare-and-update) are in process.rs: Record, Records, update.
Push (ADR 0027): send writes the audit line (audit.rs), as serve does for each pull.
